textbookText: ancient seabeds. These formations, known as stromatolites, are one of the oldest forms of life on Earth. The microorganisms trap and bind sediments (like sand and mud) to form these layers. Over time, minerals in the water stick to these layers, making them hard and rocklike. Scientists believe they might hold clues about how life started on Earth.

A. Tick the correct alternative. a) Which elements formed the Earth's core according to the Dust and cloud hypothesis? a. Aluminium, silicon, phosphorus, sulphur b. Iron, nickel, zinc, sodium c. Helium, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen d. Carbon, silicon, oxygen, sulphur
2. According to the Theory of biogenesis, where did life originate from? a. Supernatural power b. Inanimate matter c. Pre-existing life d. Another planet

3. Which theory is widely accepted as the modern explanation for the origin of life on Earth? a. Theory of special creation b. Theory of spontaneous generation c. Theory of cosmogeny d. Theory of biochemical origin of life
4. During which phase of the origin of life does the formation of complex organic molecules from simpler inorganic molecules primarily occur? a. Chemogeny b. Biogeny c. Cognogeny d. Photosynthesis
5. What is the main source of energy for the chemical reactions involved in the formation of complex organic molecules during chemogeny? a. Geothermal heat

b. Solar radiation c. Volcanic eruptions d. Atmospheric pressure 6. In which phase of the origin of life do nucleic acids like DNA and RNA first form? a. Chemogeny b. Biogeny c. Cognogeny d. Photosynthesis
7. What process enabled the transition of simple molecules to autotrophic life forms during the origin of life? a. Chemosynthesis b. Photosynthesis c. Oxidative phosphorylation d. Fermentation

8. Which gases were used in the Miller-Urey experiment to simulate the atmosphere of early Earth? a. Oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide b. Hydrogen, methane, ammonia c. Helium, argon, neon d. Carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide
9. What was the main observation from the Miller-Urey experiment? a. Formation of rocks b. Production of metals c. Synthesis of organic compounds d. Generation of volcanic ash
